pr.title: Remove global `next_disambiguator` state and handle it with a `DisambiguatorState` type
pr.description:
This removes `Definitions.next_disambiguator` as it doesn't guarantee deterministic def paths when `create_def` is called in parallel. Instead a new `DisambiguatorState` type is passed as a mutable reference to `create_def` to help create unique def paths. `create_def` calls with distinct  `DisambiguatorState` instances must ensure that that the def paths are unique without its help.

Anon associated types did rely on this global state for uniqueness and are changed to use (method they're defined in + their position in the method return type) as the `DefPathData` to ensure uniqueness. This also means that the method they're defined in appears in error messages, which is nicer.

`DefPathData::NestedStatic` is added to use for nested data inside statics instead of reusing `DefPathData::AnonConst` to avoid conflicts with those.

cc @oli-obk
pr.author: Zoxc

processing.reason: The PR changes only def-path/disambiguator bookkeeping and diagnostic expectations; it does not change any executable MIR value assignment. In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs`, `MakeByMoveBody` is untouched and `create_def` only gains a fresh `DisambiguatorState`. For the by-move synthetic body, the old global counter and the new per-query state both allocate the same `(parent_def_id, DefPathData::SyntheticCoroutineBody)` key with disambiguator 0: the query runs once per parent and is the sole creator of that `DefPathData`, so the old comment's `{closure#1}` expectation is not an executable semantic guarantee. The other changes rename anon-assoc-type def paths (method-qualified) and give nested statics a distinct `DefPathData`; these alter symbols/diagnostics/DefPathHash/metadata, not runtime values. Modeling the counter as an integer would only reproduce internal compiler bookkeeping, and manufacturing a duplicate path by giving distinct `DisambiguatorState`s the same `(parent, data)` pair would violate the PR's explicit precondition that such callers ensure uniqueness themselves. Therefore no concrete source-grounded original/transformed pair with different defined Rust program values can be validated for this PR.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: Relying on the process-global `Definitions.next_disambiguator` counter/order to assign the synthetic by-move coroutine body def path, expecting the body to become `{closure#1}` because the original coroutine is `{closure#0}`. This is incorrect because the PR states the global state "doesn't guarantee deterministic def paths when `create_def` is called in parallel". Equivalently, reusing a `DisambiguatorState` across independent `create_def` callers without ensuring distinct `(parent, DefPathData)` pairs can produce duplicate or order-dependent def paths. The corrected transformation instead supplies a fresh `DisambiguatorState::new()` because the query is called once per `parent_def_id` and is the only location creating `SyntheticCoroutineBody` for that parent.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust coroutine/generator bodies whose by-move variant is requested through the StateTransform query `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id`; the relevant input is any coroutine parent `DefId` for which the pass creates a synthetic `SyntheticCoroutineBody` definition. The broader domain also includes parallel compilation/query execution where multiple `create_def` calls can occur concurrently, and any pass that creates defs with repeated `(parent, DefPathData)` keys.
analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs`, `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` clones the coroutine body, applies `MakeByMoveBody`, then creates the synthetic by-move body definition with `tcx.create_def(parent_def_id, None, DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody)`. The old comment states: "This will always be `{closure#1}`, since the original coroutine is `{closure#0}`." Thus the synthetic body's uniqueness/disambiguator was implicitly supplied by the global `Definitions.next_disambiguator` map inside `create_def`, not by any per-query state or by a unique `(parent, DefPathData)` pair supplied by this pass.
pitfalls: Do not assume a synthetic def will receive a particular global sequence number such as `{closure#1}`; the removed global `next_disambiguator` made this order-dependent and non-deterministic under parallel create_def.

A fresh `DisambiguatorState::new()` is only safe because the StateTransform query is called once per `parent_def_id` and is the sole creator of `SyntheticCoroutineBody` for that parent; this reasoning does not generalize to multiple creators under the same parent/data pair.
Do not reuse `DefPathData::AnonConst` for nested statics: the PR adds `DefPathData::NestedStatic` specifically 'to avoid conflicts with those'.

Anonymous associated types no longer rely on global state for uniqueness; their DefPathData now includes the method name and their position in the method return type, so expectations of bare `{anon_assoc#0}` paths are stale.
Changing DefPathData affects DefPathHash, symbol mangling, CFI type-id encoding, MIR dumps, and diagnostics; test expectations must be updated consistently.
preconditions: The StateTransform by-move coroutine body pass is invoked for a coroutine parent DefId.
The pass needs to create a new LocalDefId for DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody.
No two independent callers may rely on a shared/global counter for unique def paths when create_def can run in parallel.

If multiple defs with the same parent and DefPathData are created, the same DisambiguatorState must be used; if distinct DisambiguatorState instances are used, the parent and data pair must itself be unique.
analysis.summary: StateTransform's by-move coroutine body used to obtain its synthetic def path from the global `Definitions.next_disambiguator` counter, assuming it would be `{closure#1}`. That global state does not guarantee deterministic def paths under parallel `create_def` calls. The fix makes disambiguation explicit via `DisambiguatorState`; the by-move pass uses a fresh state because the query runs once per parent and is the only creator of `SyntheticCoroutineBody` for that parent.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused regression tests that assert generated def paths/symbols and diagnostics rather than source semantics alone. For the anonymous-associated-type part of the patch, assert the new method-qualified path form (e.g. `ATrait::rpitit::{anon_assoc#0}`, `<AStruct as ATrait>::rpitit::{anon_assoc#0}`, `<T as Foo>::hello::{anon_assoc#0}`) and update .stderr expectations. For StateTransform, exercise coroutines requiring a by-move body and inspect the synthetic body's def path/MIR source (via MIR dump or stable-MIR-style def inspection) to verify it is unique and stable for the coroutine parent; run under parallel compilation/query execution to check determinism. Also cover nested statics to ensure they use `NestedStatic` rather than colliding with `AnonConst`. No compiler was built here, so these are proposed tests, not executed results.
analysis.trigger: The `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` StateTransform query runs for a coroutine and reaches the point of registering a synthetic by-move body via `tcx.create_def(parent_def_id, None, DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody, ...)`. The issue is exposed when def creation occurs in parallel or when uniqueness is assumed from global counter order instead of being guaranteed by the pass's own `(parent, DefPathData)` uniqueness.
